column2: A situation where the truth stepped out for a smoke, and a convincing version took its place.
Trading goods directly: a way to get someone else's stuff, part with yours, and pretend that was the plan all along.
Finding the exact dimensions of something — especially unpleasant when it involves your waistline.
The outer circular edge of a wheel that holds its shape and absorbs every surprise the road throws at it.
A long line of supply wagons — logistics before lorries and satnavs were invented.
An old feudal tax paid in money or goods that a peasant had zero chance of dodging.
A ring for your waist, gymnastics or a wooden barrel — depending on who or what needs holding together.
The spot where the ground abruptly calls it a day and tests your situational awareness.
A solemn sequence of actions whose deeper meaning is sometimes known only to the host.
The everyday armour saving your feet from hot tarmac, puddles and questionable fashion choices.
How much space an object takes up — suspiciously high in a suitcase right before a holiday.
A shape resembling a circle that someone gently pulled by the cheeks.
A cereal grain any horse would rate higher than a Michelin-starred restaurant.
A traditional wooden outbuilding for drying grain sheaves — the rustic ancestor of the tumble dryer.
A persistent biting fly whose main hobby is ruining summer afternoons.
Plant-based food your parents still insist you eat, even when you're well into adulthood.
A deep, narrow gorge carved by water — nature's trap for distracted hikers.
The element that warms, lights and strictly refuses to tolerate carelessness.
A grand, solemn poem placing its subject onto a verbal pedestal.
A painful reminder to test whether something is hot before grabbing it with both hands.
A body of water without ocean waves, yet boasting its own shores and occasional mosquitoes.
An involuntary shiver signalling that your body has switched to 'find a blanket immediately' mode.
A pungent gas best appreciated high up in the stratosphere rather than at nose level.
A vast expanse of salt water next to which even big problems look remarkably small.
A chemical compound formed with oxygen — an encounter that frequently ends in rust.
A transparent portal to the street, and occasionally the primary screen for watching the neighbours.
A dug-out defensive ditch — hardly the cosiest option in country real estate.
A striped freshwater fish prized as both an angler's trophy and a cat's dinner.
A graceful woodland animal with branching antlers and a seasonal side hustle pulling sleighs.
A small Mediterranean fruit capable of turning pizza toppings into a heated debate.
The mythical mountain home of the Greek gods — an exclusive address with aheavenly view.
A global sporting event where medals aren't awarded for yelling advice from the sofa.
A protective liquid coating that keeps wood looking sharp and unbothered by time.
A soft silvery metal familiar from solder wire and vintage toy soldiers.
A waterside tree that thrives in damp soil without needing applause from a gardener.
A luxury marine crustacean — essentially a prawn that really climbed the corporate ladder.
A parasitic festive plant under which kissing is traditional — botany with a romantic subtext.
Beaten eggs transformed via frying pan into a breakfast with culinary ambitions.
A deep, swirling eddy in a river best avoided without strong swimming skills and a solid reason.
A banded ornamental stone looking as though nature took a crash course in graphic design.
An iridescent gemstone that needs zero Instagram filters to show off.
A bubbly yeast mixture that works behind the scenes to help bread dough rise to fame.
Looking after someone who needs support — occasionally bundled with an excess of unsolicited advice.
A reliable stronghold or sturdy pillar standing as the last line of defence against chaos.
A survey of public opinion proving that everyone has an expert view on everything.
A numbered musical or literary work in a composer's catalogue — creativity with a passport.
The wisdom that arrives right after making a mistake — though sometimes the mistake visits twice.
A wild, unrestrained feast or revelry — definitely not a quiet evening with a cup of tea, a popular plot in films of a specific genre.
A massive crowd or warband — when too many guests arrive and it stops being a party.
A glowing ring around a light source, or a symbolic aura hovering over someone's reputation.
A newly uncovered truth or invention, often starting with the words, 'What if we try this?'
A striped insect with a sharp sting and a bad attitude that never waits for a picnic invitation.
The prolonged encirclement of a fortress — testing the attackers' patience against the defenders' pantry.
The season when leaves abandon the trees and humans dig out jumpers and philosophical thoughts.
A large, ancient fish famous for prized caviar and a distinctly serious expression.
A woodland tree whose leaves tremble constantly even when there's nothing to be afraid of.
The movement of solvent molecules through a semipermeable membrane — chemistry across borders.
An individual representative of a species — sounding far more dignified in biology than 'one random example'.
A grass-like wetland plant easily mistaken for ordinary lawn grass, though it takes no offence.
The entrance space where shoes come off, keys vanish, and guests quietly judge your tidiness.
A formal reception room for entertaining guests, where the sofa works overtime.
A writing desk with a hinged sloping flap — furniture built to keep secrets and paperwork tidy.
A prickly weed growing with such enthusiasm you'd think it gets a bonus for conquering the garden.
A dreaded historical infectious disease finally defeated by global vaccination.
The compass direction where the sun rises, abbreviated for sailors and mapmakers.
The structural skeleton of a building or ship — what remains once everything decorative is stripped away.
The central, most resilient backbone of a team — the ones who don't scatter when things get tough.
An intelligent marine mammal that looks as though it's smiling even during serious business.
A slope of loose, broken rock fragments where a mountain has shed a bit of its weight.
An imaginary line around which something rotates — literally in geometry or figuratively in life.
A large group of sheep under a shepherd's watch — a woolly meeting with no agenda.
Picking the best candidates, after which everyone else is told they were 'a very close second'.
Liquid simmered with herbs, roots or meat — essentially soup without grand culinary ambitions.
A weighted line used by builders to reveal true verticality versus wishful thinking.
A reply to a question — occasionally short, often beginning with 'Well, that's complicated.'
A division of a company with its own mission, manager and unique definition of 'urgent'.
A well-earned pause from work that some people still manage to turn into a full-time job.
Puffiness caused by fluid building up in tissues — the body deciding to scale things up slightly.
Temporary accommodation where the towels always look suspiciously whiter than the ones at home.
The parent who can fix almost anything — or at least tap it confidently with a screwdriver.
An angled embankment or incline — geometry with zero interest in staying flat.
The person convincing you to do ten more reps when your mind is already halfway home.
A firm, decisive pushback against someone stepping well over the line.
A measured length of uncut fabric sitting on a tailor's table with big plans for the future.
A young lad in old-fashioned prose — a teenager from the era before smartphones and headphones.
An organised team sharing a common goal and, ideally, the same understanding of the orders.
A formal account of completed work — the fine art of explaining where all the time went.
Your mother's husband from a subsequent marriage.
A building where people commute every morning just to send emails to one another.
A natural earthy yellow-brown pigment trusted by artists since cave-painting days.
The fireplace at the heart of a home — the historical centre of warmth and late-night conversation.
A short piece of non-fiction capturing real events or people — a portrait painted in words.
A strictly measured allowance of food calculated to keep dreams of seconds purely theoretical.
A young court attendant starting his career right next to royal intrigue.
A narrow channel cut into wood or metal to join parts together — carpentry's version of Lego.
A shopping carrier that mysteriously multiplies inside a kitchen drawer once brought home.
Coarse plant fibre used for caulking gaps — a builder's way of telling a draught to shut up.
A flat-woven floor covering that brightens a room while collecting dust with admirable discipline.
A famous Russian style of intricate miniature lacquer painting fitting an entire fairy tale onto a tiny box.
A flexible digit on your hand — indispensable for hitting 'snooze' for five more minutes.
Warm outerwear for chilly weather whose pockets regularly host forgotten coins and receipts.
A statue or structure honouring a person or event — widely regarded by pigeons as personal real estate.
Artificial hair allowing you to change your hairstyle faster than your mood.
A boat carrying passengers and cars across water wherever a bridge wasn't invited.
A classroom table where generations of pupils learned to write and doodled in the margins.
A large sheet of canvas catching the wind and turning thin air into forward motion.
A heavy, luxurious fabric woven with raised metallic patterns — strictly for grand entrances.
Kicking or throwing the ball to a teammate — sport's polite way of saying, 'Here, it's your problem now.'
A steady tropical wind that reliably pushed sailing ships across oceans for centuries.
A gripping hand tool built to hold onto bolts long after your fingers have given up.
A thick, spreadable mixture — a word equally at home in the kitchen and the bathroom cabinet.
The central Christian spring festival celebrating the Resurrection with painted eggs and a family feast.
A brief halt in speech, music or action — often the most expressive part of a conversation.
Solemn, dramatic intensity when an everyday thought is delivered as if discovering a new continent.
Ploughed farmland prepped for sowing — soil dressed up before the agricultural season begins.
A theatrical buffoon or jester paid to keep the audience laughing even on a gloomy day.
Someone turning lyrics and melody into song — occasionally doubling as the neighbours' alarm clock.
A doctor treating children who knows how to examine patients hiding behind their mum's legs.
A painting or view of natural scenery that an artist decided to keep longer than a walk lasts.
A rich, buttery tree nut that is dangerously easy to eat far more of than you intended.
